adjudications.answer: Below 768px (window.innerWidth/matchMedia) the sidebar is not rendered until the header hamburger (aria-label 'Open navigation') sets open=true. adjudications.answer: The source never sets aria-current explicitly. All nav links are react-router-dom NavLink, which by library default adds aria-current='page' on the active link (library behaviour, not verified at runtime). Visual indication: desktop rows and sub-links get 'bg-sky-500/15 text-sky-400' when active; on mobile, sub-links get font-semibold but top-level rows have no active styling. Parent rows use prefix matching, so /alerts stays 'active' on /alerts/:id; Overview and Regulatory use `end`. On /outages or /monitoring the parent 'Alerts' row is not marked active (prefix does not match).
adjudications.question: 2e. Navigation: current-page indication (aria-current)

adjudications.answer: Controls per row: select toggle (button, aria-label 'Select record'/'Deselect record'), AI-suggest (icon-only, title 'Ask AI for a recommendation', no aria-label), Accept (visible text), Reject (visible text), Skip (icon-only, aria-label 'Skip'). Header when rows are selected: 'Approve all', 'Reject all', 'Skip all'; plus 'Select all on page'/'Deselect all'. All are native <button>s, so Tab/Enter/Space work. Global window shortcuts: J/K or arrows move a visual cursor, A/R/S decide the cursor row; ignored only inside input/textarea/combobox/contenteditable. Confirmation: none for single, keyboard or batch decisions; no undo. Optimistic removal with rollback on error (lib/hooks.js:89-101). Failure reporting: a thrown error (401 or network/timeout) shows a destructive toast titled only 'Decision failed' — the error message, which distinguishes 'key missing' from 'key rejected', is discarded. Any other HTTP status is NOT detected: postDecision returns res.json() without checking res.ok, so a 400/404/500 with a JSON body yields the success toast 'Marked <decision>'. Batch reports 'N items processed' regardless of individual failures. Toasts have no live region. Persistence: the backend keeps decisions only in the module-level dict `_decisions` ('survives only until server restart'); nothing is written to outputs/review_queue.json or any ledger, no actor is recorded, and 'skip' is stored but not excluded from GET /review-queue, so a skipped row reappears after the refetch. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when that env var is set, otherwise open.
adjudications.question: 3a. Review Queue (/review): decision controls, names, keyboard, confirmation, failed-write reporting, persistence

adjudications.answer: Controls: decision-state filter Select (aria-label 'Filter by decision state'); candidate list of <button aria-pressed>; form with labelled 'Actor' text input and 'Rationale' textarea; three buttons with visible text — 'Approve', 'Reject' (destructive variant), 'Mark needs review'. All native controls, keyboard operable; no shortcuts. Guards instead of a confirmation dialog: all three are disabled until actor and rationale are non-empty and while submitting; Approve is additionally disabled when the candidate has contradictions (reason exposed only as a title attribute). No confirm step and no undo, but a later decision can overwrite. Failure reporting: postRegulatoryLinkDecision throws on 401 (key missing vs rejected), 422 (lists contradiction details) and any other non-2xx ('Decision failed (status)'), and the page shows a destructive toast 'Decision failed' with err.message; rationale is kept on failure and cleared on success. Network errors also reach the catch. Toast has no live region. Read failures are masked: list fetch failures return an empty list so the page says 'No candidates match the current filter'. Persistence: NOT memory-only — the handler writes the decided row (decision_state, decided_at, decided_by, decision_rationale) through write_regulatory_links, which schema-validates and rewrites the links JSONL. Authorization: Bearer API_SECRET_KEY when set.
adjudications.question: 3b. Regulatory Review (/regulatory/review): decision controls, names, keyboard, confirmation, failed-write reporting, persistence

adjudications.answer: Assets: yes — the same page mounts AssetsTable beside the map (keyboard-selectable rows opening the same detail sheet) and /assets offers the full table with an 'unmapped only' filter; the map footer states mapped vs unmapped counts. adjudications.question: 4d. GIS: non-map alternative for the same data

adjudications.answer: /map: no handling for basemap, glyph or terrain tile failure — the only map 'error' listener filters to NWS overlay sources and ignores everything else; there is no offline/blank-basemap message and no try/catch around map construction. Data layers are attached on 'style.load' rather than 'load' so they still draw when raster tiles never arrive (stated in a code comment). NWS overlays do report per-overlay loading/live/error text in an aria-live region, and tile URLs carry a 5-minute cache-busting bucket. Data-fetch failure: event density shows the error with a 'Retry density' button; rainfall error text is passed in as a prop; assets/municipios/alerts/gauges GeoJSON failures silently become empty FeatureCollections (getJSON fallback) and the map just shows fewer features. /monitoring HydroMapWorkspace: construction is wrapped in try/catch ('Map unavailable: …'), every map error (including tile errors) is collected into a role=alert list (max 6), and the offline export shows an explicit placeholder. Overview SVG map: no tiles; shows 'Municipal geometry is unavailable.' when geometry is missing and a contract warning when not exactly 78 features.
adjudications.question: 4e. GIS: tile / network failure handling

adjudications.answer: Pipeline.jsx uses cards, not a table. Container 'max-w-7xl mx-auto px-4 py-8 space-y-8' (:101); stats row 'flex flex-wrap gap-4' (:110); domain chips 'flex flex-wrap gap-2' (:129) so the 8 chips wrap rather than scroll; list 'grid gap-3 md:grid-cols-2' (:157), i.e. one column below Tailwind md (768px) and two above; badges 'flex flex-wrap' (:58). There is no overflow-x handling on the page. The shell collapses at 820px (AppShell.module.css:185-188) and sets min-width:0 on workspace/main (AppShell.module.css:113-115; adaptation.css:4-5). Overflow risk is present by source reading: below md the grid has a single implicit auto track and each card link is a grid item with 'block' but no min-w-0 (:49); the title inside is 'truncate' i.e. nowrap (:53) and the min-w-0 sits on an inner flex child (:52), which does not reduce the grid item's content-based minimum. A long title can therefore widen the track beyond the viewport; at md and above grid-cols-2 uses minmax(0,1fr) and the problem disappears. This matches the mobile-only overflow recorded in docs/A11Y_AUDIT.md:59-61, though that document attributes it to the chip bar, which does wrap. Not run, so this is an inference from CSS rules. PipelineItemDetail also has a 'grid grid-cols-2' metadata block with an unbroken monospace item_id (PipelineItemDetail.jsx:146-147) that can spill at narrow widths.
adjudications.question: Pipeline page responsiveness at narrow widths; horizontal overflow risk?

adjudications.answer: Labels: each checkbox is wrapped in a <label> with visible text (Handoff.jsx:106-111) inside a fieldset with legend 'Destinos' (:102-103); the legend is identical on every card and does not name the item. Focus management: none; after a successful send, load() flips loading and ListState replaces the list with skeletons, unmounting the focused button (Handoff.jsx:63, :29, :84; ListState.jsx:28-36). Error announcement: POST errors render in a span with role=alert (:131); there is no aria-live for success or partial messages (:132-133), and the success message is keyed to 'delivered', which the backend never returns (dispatch.py:259 returns pending_ack/partial/failed), so a successful send shows nothing. The list-load error branch (:31-33) is unreachable because getHandoffs returns [] on failure (pipelineClient.js:46). Loading is announced through ListState role=status (ListState.jsx:30). Button names: text 'Entregar' / 'Entregando…' (:129), not unique per item; disabled while sending or with no target selected (:127). dry_run: defaults to false on both sides. The client sends dry_run: Boolean(options.dryRun) (pipelineClient.js:63) and Handoff passes no options (Handoff.jsx:61); the backend model default is False (server/backend/main.py:148). There is no dry-run control and no confirmation step, so Entregar performs a live repository dispatch.

adjudications.answer: References: the exception itself at .federation/gui-capabilities.json:1747-1768 (owner jotaele44, tracking jotaele44/thehub-pr#56, expires 2027-01-31, renewed 2026-11-15; candidate_ids are GET /{case_id}, GET /{case_id}/{collection}, POST /{case_id}/claims, POST /{case_id}/claims/{claim_id}/evidence-relations); a copy in the generated artifacts/gui-capabilities-merged.json:2256; and one mention in .federation/gui-capabilities.extensions/case-manager-authorization-boundary.json:9. Measures by category (config/financial_category_ontology.json): contract_award=AWARDED (sum of award_amount, server/backend/leaderboard_adapters.py:218,237,247); debt_issuance=DEBT_ISSUED_PAR; asg_emergency_purchase_source_native=ASG_EMERGENCY_PURCHASE_COST; federal_obligation / federal_grant / disaster_assistance / federal_assistance=OBLIGATED (sum of obligated_amount, lines 773,784); campaign_contribution_received=CONTRIBUTIONS_RECEIVED (sum of amount, lines 933,947); 13 further categories (PAID, FUNDED, LOAN_PRINCIPAL, GUARANTEED, etc.) have no adapter and return zero rows. There is no 'disbursement' or 'payment' ranking with data. Null handling: records with a missing amount are excluded and counted under 'Excluded' in the Reconciliation panel (adapters 219-221; UI line 109); missing currency -> 'Unresolved'; a category with no rows shows the sentence 'No certifiable ranking rows for this category. Missing adapters or source manifestations remain explicit rather than becoming false zero rankings.' (line 101), not a zero. Missing state badges render 'UNKNOWN' (line 14); candidateCount and snapshot count default to 0 (lines 98, 105). CAMPAIGN FINANCE. (i) Tile 'Signed amount' = summary.totalContributionAmount (dashboard/src/components/CampaignFinance.jsx:137); '—' if null, but the backend always returns a number (0 when nothing is materialized). (ii) Contributions table column 'Amount' = row.amount via fmtMoney (lines 36, 47): FEC contribution_receipt_amount or CEE/OCE amount (server/backend/campaign_finance.py:162,181). (iii) Entities table column 'Amount' = row.amount (lines 67, 78), which the backend sets only for recipient rows, from total_disbursements (server/backend/campaign_finance.py:269); candidate and committee rows carry no amount and render '—'. (iv) 'Federal outflows' tile is a row COUNT of FEC disbursements + independent expenditures, not money (line 140; server/backend/campaign_finance.py:121); 'Contribution rows', 'FEC', 'CEE + OCE' are also counts (default 0). Missing text fields render '—'. OWNERSHIP. No monetary field is displayed. Columns are Shares (integer), '% issuer' (percent_issuer_shares_computed) and '13F portfolio %' (percent_13f_reportable_value) (dashboard/src/components/OwnershipDeepDive.jsx:92-94, 108-110); null -> '—' via fmtInt/fmtPct (lines 15-23). market_value exists in the payload builder (moneysweep/capital_control/deep_dive.py:290) but is not rendered. Metric tiles are counts/states, defaulting to 0 or '—' (lines 59-64). PLACES WHERE DIFFERENT KINDS OF AMOUNT SHARE A LABEL OR ARE SUMMED (reported, not judged): (a) Campaign Finance uses the single label 'Amount' for contribution receipts in the Contributions view and for recipients' total_disbursements in the Entities view (dashboard/src/components/CampaignFinance.jsx:36 vs 67; server/backend/campaign_finance.py:162/181 vs 269). (b) 'Signed amount' adds FEC receipts + CEE amounts + OCE amounts into one figure across three sources (server/backend/campaign_finance.py:103-105, 120). (c) In the contributions feed a blank or unparseable amount is coerced to 0 by _amount (server/backend/campaign_finance.py:58-62) before reaching the UI, so a missing contribution amount displays as '$0', not '—'; the same coercion feeds the 'Signed amount' sum. This differs from Contracts, where blank stays null and shows '—'. (d) Top Entities shows awarded, obligated, debt-par, purchase-cost and contributions-received values under one 'Value' header, one category at a time; nothing in the UI sums across categories, and the measure is named in the caption. (e) The ASG emergency-purchase adapter reads a column named obligation_amount and reports it with metricType ASG_EMERGENCY_PURCHASE_COST (server/backend/leaderboard_adapters.py:406, 467, 480). (f) federal_assistance and disaster_assistance pool several source programmes (grants, fema_pa, fema_hmgp, cdbg_dr, hud, ...) into one OBLIGATED total per UEI (server/backend/leaderboard_adapters.py:840-871); fema_pa/fema_hmgp/cdbg_dr records are counted in both categories. (g) Outside the four views asked about: Municipios shows an unlabelled dollar figure that is the sum of award_amount per municipio, '—' when none are populated (dashboard/src/components/MunicipalityAggregates.jsx:51; server/backend/main.py:239-245), and Relationships shows an unlabelled edge amount only when non-null (dashboard/src/components/RelationshipGraph.jsx:42).
adjudications.question: 4. Financial semantics in Contracts, Top Entities, Campaign Finance and Ownership: fields, labels, null rendering, mixed amounts.

adjudications.answer: Recently opened items: NONE FOUND. Pinned items: NONE FOUND. User rename of any object: NONE FOUND. The only browser storage the app touches is one localStorage key prefix, federation.programActivity.v1.<producerId> (dashboard/src/components/programActivityEvent.js:3), read by readLiveProgramActivity (line 51) to merge activity events into the Activity tab. Its writer appendProgramActivityEvent (line 64) has no caller in dashboard/src outside its test. It holds activity events, not a recents or pins list. The prebuilt desktop bundle (desktop/prebuilt-dashboard/bundle/assets/index-xHPKZVps.js) contains the same key and no other localStorage key. No sessionStorage or IndexedDB use was found. Desktop: the only remembered user choice is the single workspace folder picked in the external Setup & Diagnostics centre. It is applied from saved state at launch (desktop/launch.py:33-43; desktop/config.py:34-37). It is one saved value, not a list of recent workspaces, and its UI lives in the external prii_desktop package, which is not in the snapshot. Rename: there are no PATCH routes on any backend, and the case manager has only create/command POSTs (server/backend/case_manager_api.py:200-374), with case_id derived deterministically from title/type/scope (server/backend/case_manager_api.py:203), so a case title cannot be renamed. The dashboard has no rename or edit-label control. Searched (case-insensitive): localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB and recent|pinned|pin|favorite|favourite|bookmark|rename over dashboard/src, desktop/*.py, desktop/prebuilt-dashboard bundle and server/backend/*.py. Every match outside the program-activity module was in a test (programActivityEvent.test.js, cs-format.test.js), and the 'renamed' match there is test data for an event title.

adjudications.answer: Confirmed, exactly six, in this order in the WORKSPACES registry: Chat -> ChatView; Workbench -> WorkbenchWorkspace; Sources -> SourcesWorkspace; Memory -> MemoryWorkspace; Provenance -> ProvenanceWorkspace; Settings -> SettingsWorkspace. Each is rendered only when health.state is 'ok' and view equals its id. 'Background tasks' is a seventh item in the same nav list but opens a drawer, not a workspace. While the service wants a token, TokenGate replaces all six.
adjudications.question: 1. Six workspaces: exact list and mounted component for each

adjudications.answer: Functional but read-only and narrow; not presentational. It has no props, no buttons, inputs, links or handlers of its own: the only controls are one native <details>/<summary> 'Record' per tool call. On mount it makes two calls. GET /tools/summary returns counts by status computed from the stored tool-call records plus a live verification of the hash-chained audit log; the UI shows 'Verified (N events)' or the broken status and reason in error styling. GET /tools/requests returns every stored tool call; the UI lists them newest first with status, tool name, created time and, behind the disclosure, requested_by, approved_by, denied_by, argument digest, run id and raw arguments/result JSON. Both are real persisted data. Limits: loaded once (no refresh, filter, pagination, loading state or link to the run); the audit events themselves (GET /tools/audit) are never shown; 'who decided' is the constant 'api' for every GUI decision and 'policy:auto-local-read-only' for auto approvals; it shows nothing about source provenance, message-edit originals (which the chat UI says are 'preserved in provenance') or execution-entry receipts. Acceptance ledger is _architecture/release/acceptance_ledger_v1.json. TGT-032 'Provenance inspection' (IMPLEMENTED / PASS, note 'Verified audit chain, per-action records behind disclosure') matches the component exactly; its positive gate is a rendered check that waits for 'Verified (N events)' and then records a literal true. TGT-014 'Governed tool execution' lists the component and is supported by a rendered check that the Record shows requested_by 'model'. TGT-003 'Specialized workspaces' (PARTIAL / OPEN) says 'Sources/Memory/Settings exist; GIS/OCR/Code/Provenance/Artifacts surfaces absent': stale and contradicted by current source and by TGT-032, since Provenance and Workbench are both mounted. INV-018 'Provenance' (PARTIAL / PROVISIONAL) is about backend provenance records on ingested sources, not this workspace; those records are shown in the Evidence sheet and Sources detail, not here. MATRIX-015 lists provenance among 70 rendered checks; no axe run covers the Provenance view. No acceptance or ledger entries about Provenance were found in .mucaro/ or qa/ other than the rendered script.
adjudications.question: 2. Provenance workspace: fully functional, partial or presentational; ledger reconciliation

adjudications.answer: Three media rules. (a) max-width 760px: single-column shell, off-canvas sidebar, top bar with hamburger, tighter paddings, execution-entry buttons stretch to 44px, user bubble 92% wide, and every Sheet becomes a bottom sheet (full width, max-height 88vh, rounded top). (b) max-width 900px or pointer:coarse: 16px form fields and 44px minimum control height. (c) prefers-reduced-motion. Safe-area insets are applied to sidebar, top bar, composer and sheet body. The native window minimum (420x560) is below 760px, so the desktop app shows the phone layout when narrowed. The workspace switcher has no separate mobile form: it is the same six buttons inside the off-canvas sidebar, reached through the hamburger; picking one closes the panel. Background tasks is a button in that panel (and in the conversation menu); on a narrow screen it opens as a bottom sheet over the page, with focus trap, Escape and backdrop close from Sheet. No workspace has its own breakpoint rules; they rely on flex wrapping. Gaps: the closed panel stays focusable (see accessibility findings), no Escape or close button for the panel, composer Enter inserts a newline on coarse pointers by design. Rendered evidence exists for 390x844 and 393/430/720 widths only; nothing renders at 420x560, and the ledger marks software-keyboard avoidance OPEN (MOB-F01).
adjudications.question: 3. Mobile: breakpoints and narrow-viewport behaviour (window min 420x560); workspace switcher and background-tasks drawer

adjudications.answer: Shortcuts are local only (listed in keyboard_shortcuts); there are no global accelerators and none for switching workspace. Composer: Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a newline, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter always sends; on a coarse pointer Enter is a newline and only the button or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends. IME safe: the handler returns early when event.nativeEvent.isComposing is true or keyCode is 229. Empty text cannot be sent; focus returns to the textarea after sending. Focus order follows the DOM: skip link, sidebar (New chat, six workspaces, Background tasks, filter, conversations), then main (hamburger on narrow screens, service banner Retry, workspace content); in Chat: Model, Repository, conversation menu, feed controls, queued items, textarea, Mode, Stop, Send. All six workspaces and the tasks drawer are native buttons, so every workspace is reachable by keyboard alone at desktop width. At <=760px they are still reachable, but through an off-screen panel whose focus is invisible unless the hamburger is pressed first. View changes do not move focus.
adjudications.question: 4. Keyboard: shortcuts, composer behaviour, focus order, reachability

adjudications.answer: Eleven overlays, all built on one Sheet component: Background tasks, Tool activity, Evidence [n] (right drawers / bottom sheets); Rename conversation, Delete conversation?, Remove this source?, Delete this memory?, Revoke folder access?, Save answer, Execution receipt, Adjust goal / Revise plan (centred). Sheet gives each role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby pointing at its h2 title, a labelled close button, initial focus on a data-autofocus field or the dialog itself, a Tab/Shift+Tab trap, Escape to close, backdrop mousedown to close, and focus return to the element focused at mount. Confirm sheets focus the cancel button and ignore close while busy. Weaknesses: the background is not inert; the trap selector omits summary and can pick hidden elements; focus return fails when the opener was a menu item that has unmounted. Three overlays are not dialogs: the mobile navigation panel, the conversation menu (role=menu) and the mode picker (role=listbox); none has Escape, a trap or focus return. The inline 'Confirm Directory Access' block is not a dialog.
adjudications.question: 5. Modals/drawers: role, aria-modal, labelling, focus trap, Escape, focus return

adjudications.answer: Rendering: the client reads server-sent events with fetch, de-duplicates by seq and concatenates text_delta events into the answer, rendered as inert text with fenced code blocks; the run article is aria-busy while RUNNING and the feed auto-scrolls only when already near the bottom. The streaming text is not a live region; 'Answer complete.' is announced at the end. Save and Share appear only on terminal runs; Copy and Edit are offered while still streaming. Cancel: Stop calls POST /work-runs/{id}/stop. Waiting runs stop at once; a running run is flagged and stops at the next phase boundary, but the answer phase has no checkpoint, so Stop does not interrupt text that is already streaming and the run still ends COMPLETED. Model/provider error mid-answer: the backend records error and final(FAILED) events; text_delta events already written stay in the log, so the partial text remains above an alert showing category, status and detail, and 'The turn failed.' is announced. Disconnect: a stream that fails, closes without an end event or is silent for 25 s is retried with backoff (reloading the run from the event log each time); after 10 failures a 'Live updates paused' notice with Resume appears; the app-level banner shows 'Reconnecting…' from the 15 s health poll, and returning to the page or regaining network forces a re-follow. Partial output is preserved because events are persisted server-side. A service restart marks running runs INTERRUPTED. Defect by source reading: runs with more than 500 events are reloaded truncated to the first 500 (see workflow stream-answer).
adjudications.question: 6. Streaming: rendering, cancel, mid-stream error or disconnect, partial output

adjudications.answer: Tool-request approval is complete. The card is a labelled region ('Permission request for <tool>') showing the tool, who asked, arguments (patches as a diff) and the argument digest, with native Deny and Allow once buttons. They POST /tools/requests/{id}/approve or /deny with arguments_sha256. The backend refuses a non-pending call or a digest mismatch, stores status with approved_by/denied_by and a timestamp on the tool-call record, appends a hash-chained audit event, and resumes the run. Both buttons work from the keyboard; the waiting state is announced ('Waiting for your approval.') and the decision is announced ('Allowed/Denied <tool>.') through the polite live region, and the conversation list shows 'Needs your approval'. Focus is not moved to the card and is lost when it disappears. The actor recorded is the constant 'api'. The Planning-to-Execution Gate named in README and docs/EXECUTION_GATE.md (POST /plan, POST /approve) has no GUI: the Workbench only compiles a plan with approval NOT_REQUESTED and states that nothing is executed. The GUI gate that does exist is the execution-entry card: Proceed/Execute and Adjust/Revise post a decision bound to artifact, revision, expected version, source commit and an idempotency key; the decision and receipt hashes are persisted and shown in the Execution receipt sheet. The primary button is natively disabled with an aria-describedby reason until the entry is ready and the source identity is current, it activates from the keyboard, and 'Execution started.' is announced. But the GUI can neither create an entry nor mark one ready, so this gate is usable only for entries prepared through the API.
adjudications.question: 7. Approval workflows: Planning-to-Execution Gate and tool-request approval

adjudications.answer: Evidence tier (T1-T4) is the only tier: a colour badge in the table, card, detail header and map point colour, with a legend that labels T1 'highest confidence' and T4 'lowest confidence'. There is no witness tier; witness is one plain-text line built from witness_type, count and name. 'Confidence' is a second unlabelled badge whose value is the first present of case_confidence, chronology_confidence, source_reliability - a number in the ledger - while the colour map expects high/medium/low words, so it is always slate. source_reliability, chronology_confidence, location_confidence, dedupe_status and translation_status are not displayed. Source is a citation/family/URL label, linked only for http(s) URLs, with a 'No URL' flag otherwise; source_family appears as an 'Agency involvement' badge tinted amber for military families. Review state on a master case is the review_action word inside the muted provenance line (it is 'promote' on all 470 rows). Candidates show review_status as a federation tone badge plus an evidence-tier badge.

adjudications.answer: Confirmed. The router declares only '/' and '*'. The mobile view is useState('cases'); the desktop view is an uncontrolled Radix Tabs with defaultValue 'cases' (a separate state from the mobile one, so crossing 860px resets it); the open case is a useState object; filters, page and page size are CaseGrid-local state. No file in dashboard/src uses useParams, useSearchParams or useNavigate. A view deep link would require one shared view value bound to the URL (search parameter or path segment) driving both a controlled Tabs and MobileNav, and working under HashRouter for the offline export. A case deep link would require a case id in the URL resolved either from the loaded /cases array or through GET /cases/{case_id}, which exists in the backend and as an unused client function; the offline snapshot has no per-case keys, so offline it must resolve from the /cases list. It also needs a not-found state for an unknown id, and SPA fallback for non-root paths in the desktop server, which lives in the external prii_desktop package and was not available to inspect.
adjudications.question: 4. Views are in-memory state with no URL: confirm, and state what a deep link to a view or to a single case would require.

adjudications.answer: Storage: window.localStorage key 'federation_write_token' (federationClient.js:13,18-27), plus an in-memory copy appParams.writeToken captured at module load (app-params.js:84). The only way it gets set is the URL query parameter ?write_token=..., which getParamValue writes to localStorage under federation_write_token and then strips from the URL via history.replaceState (app-params.js:35-49,84); ?clear_write_token=true removes it (app-params.js:64-66). It is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' only when no access token is present (federationClient.js:65-66,72-74). UI entry: NONE - there is no input, form or settings surface for the token; setWriteToken is exported but has no caller (grep setWriteToken in src: definition only). The backend exposes public_settings.write_token_required (main.py:1108) but the frontend never reads it, so the UI cannot prompt; the only user-facing hint is the Review-queue 401/403 message 'Reviewing needs write access (a local network, or the PRII write token).' (SkyCameras.jsx:305). Token persists in localStorage in plaintext with no expiry. The backend comment at main.py:309-312 ('browser UI has no write-credential input ... sources only the federation access token') is partly stale: the client now does source a separate write token, but still offers no input.
adjudications.question: Write-token handling: where the frontend stores the write token and whether any UI lets the user enter it

adjudications.answer: The reported defect (Finance filter comparing only raw foreign keys) is fixed: a custom globalFilterFn builds its haystack from contract id, raw agency/vendor/site ids AND agency code/name, vendor name, site name, formatted amount, status and tier, and has tests. Residual mismatches of the same family remain in current source: (a) Finance column SORT still uses the raw accessor values for Agency, Vendor and Site while the cells render code/name, so header sorting orders by V-/A-/S- ids, not by the visible text; (b) the Nearest tool's result label prefers properties.id over properties.name, and the Sites target supplies both, so the user is shown a raw site id; (c) CSV export and the evidence-brief contracts table emit raw vendor/agency/site ids where the table shows names; (d) inspector linked-contract/anomaly lists and the watchlist show ids only. The ProgramTimeline search compares against the same title/detail/category/phase strings it renders (no mismatch). The Finance KPI cards and EXPORT CSV ignore the active filter.
adjudications.question: 1. Display-name filtering against raw identifiers

adjudications.answer: The mechanism named in the old audit (whenStyleReady gated on map.isStyleLoaded) no longer exists; the runtime now resolves `ready` on the style.load event and layer hooks add sources directly. Loading is set at SI:255 (GeoJSON layers) and SI:326 (Martin vector layer); it is cleared by 'source-ready' (263/342), 'loaded' (267/352), 'error' (270/355, and 320 for tile errors) and 'idle' when toggled off (246/313). Paths on which it is NOT cleared: (1) hung request — both hooks use bare fetch with an AbortSignal but no timeout (257, 328), so a backend that accepts the connection and never answers leaves 'loading…' indefinitely; (2) abort/cancel — the catch and the post-await guards return without writing a status (260, 264, 269 / 341, 343, 354); when the cleanup is caused by a 2D→3D switch or a runtime reboot the effect re-runs with mapRef.current === null and returns at 236/303 before any onStatus call, so the last status ('loading…', 'source ready' or 'rendered') stays on the button for as long as 3D is active, and the layer buttons are still rendered in 3D (867-883) while the failure banner is 2D-only (848); (3) 'source-ready' is terminal if map.getSource(sourceId) is already true at 264/343; (4) two hooks write the same 'municipios' key: with Martin delivery the vector hook sets 'loading' and the disabled GeoJSON hook then sets 'idle' in the same commit (313 vs 246, declared at 477-496), so the button reads 'on' rather than 'loading…' until the fetch settles; (5) empty result — an empty FeatureCollection (backend returns one for any allowed layer with no file, main.py:472) is reported as 'rendered' with no empty indication; (6) vector layer 'loaded' is set when the source is added, not when tiles arrive, so missing tiles show 'rendered' unless MapLibre raises an error event carrying sourceId. Unmount is safe (state is discarded; cleanup aborts and removes layers, 275-279). Related flags with the same no-timeout weakness: gazetteer density (614-617) and the ERI catalog (spatial/imagery/eriApi.ts:65) which also suppresses URL-hash writes while loading (useImageryController.ts:135). Access-point registries use fetchWithTimeout but 'Records received; drawing…' never advances when the map is not ready (e.g. WebGL unavailable: activeMode stays 'maplibre' with ready=false, useSpatialRuntime.ts:60-70, so the panel is shown and the draw effect returns at useAccessPointsController.ts:121).
adjudications.question: 2. Map layer loading that can remain stuck

adjudications.answer: The silent-blank case is fixed in the client and covered by four tests: HTTP error → 'RAG backend returned <status>'; no body → 'returned no response stream'; done event with non-zero rc → 'RAG backend exited with code N'; rc 0 with no data lines → 'completed without producing output'; stream closed without a done event → 'ended without terminal status'; malformed done payload → 'invalid terminal status'; transport error/8 s header timeout → the exception text. Each calls onError then onDone, and QueryLayer renders a role=alert 'Query failed' card with the message plus a hint to switch to STUB; partial output stays visible below it. query_llm.py now exists at the repo root as a wrapper. What is still not useful: (a) the backend opens the subprocess with stderr=PIPE and never reads it, so the reason for a non-zero exit (traceback, missing model/dependency) never reaches the user — only the exit code does; an unread stderr pipe can also fill and block the child, in which case no done event is ever sent; (b) while pending and before the first token the panel shows nothing at all — no response card (needs streamLines.length > 0), no 'No query run yet' card (needs !pending) — only the button reading STOP; there is no overall timeout on the stream; (c) STOP/unmount only sets a cancelled flag: the fetch is not aborted and the generator has no cleanup to terminate the subprocess; (d) query_llm prints progress lines ('Loading model…', 'Retrieving relevant posts…', '====') to stdout, which are streamed to the user as answer text, and any one such line satisfies the 'produced output' check; (e) the error card persists after switching back to STUB until the next run.
adjudications.question: 3. RAG stream termination without useful feedback

adjudications.answer: Exhaustive list of deferral points in non-test source: (1) six React.lazy module chunks in App.tsx — CommandCenter, FinanceIntelligence (defers @tanstack/react-table), SpatialIntelligence (defers maplibre-gl JS, the @turf/* packages, Zod-based imagery/access-point clients via its static imports), AnomalyWorkbench, InvestigationGraph, QueryLayer — rendered inside one Suspense with a 'Loading module…' fallback and a per-module ErrorBoundary; (2) one dynamic import, RuntimeFactory.createCesiumRuntime → './CesiumRegionalRuntime', which is the only file importing 'cesium' and 'cesium/Build/Cesium/Widgets/widgets.css', so Cesium JS+CSS load only when 3D is requested; (3) MapLibre's worker is imported with ?worker&url so it is a separate emitted asset; (4) Cesium Workers/Assets/ThirdParty/Widgets are copied to public/cesium by the postinstall script and fetched at runtime via CESIUM_BASE_URL='/cesium/'. There is NO manualChunks or any build/rollupOptions block in vite.config.ts — chunking is whatever Rollup derives from the dynamic imports. Caveats that affect what 'lazy' currently means: main.tsx statically imports 'maplibre-gl/dist/maplibre-gl.css' and ten @fontsource CSS files, so MapLibre's CSS is in the entry CSS; InvestigationGraph statically imports AccessPointRelationships → accessPointsApi (Zod), and api/client.ts (entry) imports schemas/priis (Zod), so Zod is in the entry chunk; there is no graph library to defer — both graphs are hand-written SVG. Access-point relationships, the control cross-section, registry features and evidence are lazy at the data level (fetched on demand), not code-split.
adjudications.question: 4. Lazy-loading of heavy dependencies (must be preserved)

adjudications.answer: Confirmed. ModuleId is the union command|finance|spatial|anomaly|graph|query; App holds it in useState initialised to 'command' and changes it only through setModule calls from the tab strip, the left rail, the command-bar submit (→ query), Command Center's OPEN QUERY LAYER button and its anomaly cards (→ anomaly). A grep of non-test source for location/history/URLSearchParams/hashchange/popstate finds no code that derives the module from the URL and no hashchange/popstate listener anywhere; the module is not persisted to localStorage either. The only URL consumers are in the Spatial imagery controller: it parses window.location.hash once at mount for map=zoom/lat/lng, eri, op, cmp, fp, base; rewrites the fragment with history.replaceState on moveend and on imagery state changes (skipped while the catalog is loading); and copies window.location.href for 'Copy link'. formatViewHash deletes only its own six keys and preserves any other fragment keys, and the viewHash header states the fragment is free because the app has no router — so a module key in the fragment would survive, but the Spatial controller only runs while the Spatial tab is mounted and its fragment remains in the address bar after leaving the tab. eriApi also reads window.location.origin, and the root ErrorBoundary calls window.location.reload().
adjudications.question: 5. Six modules; nothing reads the URL to select one; existing use of location.hash

adjudications.answer: One place: fetchPriisDataWithFallback catches any rejection from fetchPriisData (network error, 8 s timeout, or any non-2xx on any of the nine entity endpoints) and returns the bundled priisData with live=false. App also seeds its initial state with the same mock object before the fetch resolves. The only indicator is the command-bar text LIVE vs DEMO; the classification banner says DEMO in both cases. A Zod-invalid row is dropped by parseArray rather than triggering fallback, and an empty-but-reachable backend yields live=true with empty tables. Nothing else falls back to fixtures: spatial layers, imagery, access points, RAG and pipeline surface errors instead (spatial/accessPoints/fixtures.ts is imported only by tests).
